limits: Exact native deathknightA / deathKnight / renderer 121217 source assignment only; no sibling Death Knight, resource rig, alternate renderer, or topology receives credit from this record.

The first seven ordinary zero-focus attempts preserved HP 45 and returned native Block with damage 0; attempt 8 returned native Damaged with damage 1 and reduced HP from 45 to 44. The disposable fixture capped only the equipped bluntSmithHammer Toughness attack skill at the native 0.95 cap, so the observed combat balance is not representative.
Death used the explicit KillSingle fixture for 988 damage from HP 44 to 0 and is not ordinary lethal-damage evidence.

The native death path enabled the source ragdoll: eleven retained rigidbodies became dynamic after the Death trigger, and reviewed samples show a coherent prone custom-mesh corpse. This establishes only the sampled fixture handoff and retained capture interval.
Nineteen selected original PNGs were reviewed; the remaining 1,181 captured frames and generated videos are retained evidence but were not individually reviewed.

Native effects, slot icons, the foreground hero, and the loot panel obscure portions of the attack, hit, and death sequences. No reviewed frame showed a detached authored surface, missing limb, residual stretch, obvious floor penetration, or viewport clipping outside the native attack travel above the camera.
Other native attacks, portrait, collision, extended culling, long-session resource lifetime, full campaign completion, and final art-direction approval remain outside this archive.

selectedPNGs.observation: The exact authored sentinel is fully visible at native scale in settled idle. Its horned helmet, glowing eyes, ribbed torso, mace, shield, arms, legs, and feet form a coherent armored silhouette with no sampled floor or viewport clipping.

Immediately before the native AttackProf trigger, the custom mesh remains fully assembled with the shield guarding the body and the mace held clear of the forearm. Native slot icons overlap the top of the helmet.

The opening native attack pose lifts the complete custom sentinel off the floor while its helmet, torso, limbs, mace, and shield stay connected and readable. A native ground flare covers only the lower background.

The native aerial attack advances toward the hero with both armored legs bent, the shield rotated forward, and the mace extended. The custom surface remains coherent; the hero covers part of the lower attack path.
Near the attack apex, most of the sentinel is above the viewport and only its lower legs are visible. This frame establishes native travel through the shot but cannot judge the hidden upper geometry.

The native attack resolves with the airborne sentinel visible above the struck hero. Its shield, mace, helmet, torso, and legs remain joined, while damage and daze overlays limit inspection of the lower contact area.
The sentinel returns to an upright guarded pose after the native attack with the full authored silhouette intact. The daze ring is attached to the hero and does not obscure the target.
A later settled sample again shows the complete sentinel in its native stance with no sampled residual stretch, detached surface, missing equipment, or clipping.

The first ordinary zero-focus attempt visibly resolves as BLOCKED while the sentinel lowers its shield from the native defense pose. The custom helmet, torso, weapon arm, shield arm, and legs remain connected; HP stays 45.
The eighth ordinary zero-focus attempt begins with the exact sentinel intact at HP 45. Native attack-slot UI overlaps the space between the combatants but leaves the target readable.

The causal native Damaged frame records HP 44, but the foreground hero and bright impact sphere cover most of the custom torso. The exposed helmet, horns, mace, and outside shield contour remain aligned; central deformation cannot be judged here.

The native hit recoil is visible after the one-point critical result. The sentinel bends backward with the shield raised while its head, chest, arms, mace, shield, hips, and legs remain attached; the hero covers the lower center.
The target recovers to its complete upright silhouette at HP 44 with no sampled neck gap, separated shoulder, detached equipment, missing limb, or viewport clipping.

The explicit KillSingle fixture starts from an intact sentinel at HP 44. The action panel states the native-capped 95 percent per-slot accuracy used for this disposable test, and this frame is not ordinary lethal evidence.

Immediately after the native Death trigger, the eleven retained death rigidbodies are dynamic and the custom sentinel begins its ragdoll fall. Smoke, debris, the foreground hero, and the 988 damage label obscure portions of the body.
The native ragdoll collapses behind the hero while the helmet, armored body, mace, shield, and limbs remain visually associated. Impact smoke and foreground overlap limit fine joint inspection.

The custom sentinel has settled into a readable prone ragdoll behind the hero. Its horned helmet, torso armor, shield, mace, arms, and legs form a coherent fallen arrangement without obvious floor penetration in this view.
A later unobstructed sample retains the coherent prone ragdoll and separate equipped mace on the floor while combat UI clears. This proves the sampled handoff only, not later corpse lifetime.

The gold-loot panel is open while the fallen sentinel remains visible in the blurred background. The overlay prevents fine geometry inspection and this fixture capture does not establish ordinary lethal behavior or later corpse lifetime.
